message:
test(udp): stop defaulting at the port the installed product listens on

Test 1. Both arguments are required now.

The defaults were 127.0.0.1 and 43000. That is the installed GNLink. A bare run -- which is what a
regression sweep does -- therefore dialled the user's own running host and sent it a UDP hello.
Mine did exactly that during the full sweep earlier; the host rejected it and nothing came of it,
which is the only reason this reads as a near miss rather than an incident.

A test that reaches into the live product unless told otherwise is wrong regardless of how it went
this time. There is no default any more: no arguments means usage and exit 2, the same shape the
other argument-taking programs in this directory use, and the message says what the old default
was so the reason is not lost.

This makes explicit what it always was -- a tool that needs a host you started, not a test that can
run on its own. That is also why it showed up as one of the four non-zero exits in the sweep: it
had no host to talk to. What it did have was a target, and that was the problem.
